company.name: Palewell Software
company.one_line: Project-tracking software for small consulting firms and agencies.

market.description: Project tracking for small professional-services firms, a crowded but fragmented market.

competitors.name: Trackbench
competitors.positioning: Established incumbent with a broad feature set
competitors.relative_strength: Much larger install base and brand recognition

competitors.name: Fieldnote Ops
competitors.positioning: Newer entrant targeting the same small-agency segment
competitors.relative_strength: Cheaper pricing tier that undercuts Palewell on cost-sensitive deals

situation.prompt: Palewell has 38 paying customers and no dedicated support team; when a customer's time-tracking export breaks, the founder personally fixes it, and it has happened 4 times this quarter. Do you invest engineering time in a self-serve export repair tool, or hire the company's first support hire?
situation.tension: There is no answer that is obviously right: hiring solves it faster, but permanently adds a fixed cost that a 14-person seed company has not budgeted for.
options: Hire the company's first dedicated support person
Build a self-serve export repair tool instead of hiring
Document the manual fix and defer both until the next funding round
constraints: No budget approved for a new hire this quarter
One engineer is available for two weeks before returning to the core roadmap
The founder cannot keep personally fixing exports past this quarter
situation.leadership_belief: The founder believes this is a one-off rough edge that will disappear as the export code matures, though it has recurred every few weeks since launch.

supporting_facts: The time-tracking export has broken 4 times this quarter, each requiring the founder to fix it manually.
Palewell has 38 paying customers and $412.6K in ARR.

One engineer is available for two weeks before returning to core roadmap work.
Trackbench has a materially larger install base among small consulting firms.
Fieldnote Ops undercuts Palewell's pricing for cost-sensitive deals.
